channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Walter Isaacson on curiosity and creativity in the AI age.
item.description: Walter Isaacson tells Google’s Kent Walker in Dialogues on Technology and Society that Leonardo da Vinci, Benjamin Franklin and Ada Lovelace show breakthroughs are often team efforts and curiosity plus human judgment matter more as AI makes information abundant. (Google AI Blog)

item.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
item.description: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast (OpenAI News)

item.title: S3 audit log streaming with OpenID Connect expands to GHE.com
item.description: Enterprise audit logs on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (GHE.com) can now stream to Amazon S3 via OpenID Connect, extending the github.com capability and removing the need to store long-lived AWS credentials on GitHub. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
item.description: DaisyRose-27B, RadixArk's first model built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with Miles, lifts Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 from 5.6% to 12.0% with 1,200 curated tasks over 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs, cutting training cost 57%. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Neon offers frontier-level intelligence for complex coding and analysis at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1-million-token context window and a 70.9% Vals Index score ranking second. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot for agentic coding, multistep tool use and knowledge work, with Google claiming quality close to Gemini 4 Carbon at a lower token cost per task, faster responses and fewer unrequested changes. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say
item.description: Across 272 production SFT runs, FLOP-based estimates reached only R²=0.31 and 12.41 h MAE, while CatBoost using pre-scheduling information hit R²=0.98 and 1.71 h MAE, explaining why fine-tuning often outruns FLOP predictions. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Cheaper and better at the same tasks": Microsoft openly takes on Claude and ChatGPT
item.description: At Ignite, Microsoft Commercial Business CEO Althoff claimed Copilot can do any task Claude or ChatGPT can do better and cheaper, citing over 30 million Copilot paid users and 450 million Office enterprise users as of June. (AIbase)

item.title: Connect Supabase, Box, Calendly, and more to Copilot
item.description: GitHub added eight GitHub-verified MCP connectors to Copilot in public preview, letting users ask why a Buildkite build failed and fix the code in the same session or check a Supabase schema before writing a migration. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Perfect-scoring student dies after being suspected of AI cheating; South Korean exam halls rush to ban smart glasses
item.description: Lee Jin-woo, 32, achieved a perfect LEET score, faced AI-cheating suspicions, promised a YouTube CSAT proof livestream, then died of cardiac arrest in a Seoul motel as Korean exam sites moved to ban smart glasses. (AIbase)

item.title: Wait for pull request events with GitHub CLI
item.description: GitHub CLI v2.105.0 adds GitHub Event Streams so `gh event listen` can wait on a pull request URL for events such as a submitted review, emitting JSON lines instead of polling in a loop. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Tesla's robot sets its sights on the home, with Musk saying it could clear dirty dishes and take out the trash next year
item.description: Elon Musk says Tesla’s humanoid robot Optimus is progressing well, with a real demo video planned within one to two months and hopes that in 12 to 18 months it can clear dirty dishes and take out the trash. (AIbase)

item.title: Anthropic hits Nasdaq exchanges at $111, 33% above IPO price
item.description: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share to raise more than $80 billion, then opened on Nasdaq at $111—33% above the IPO price—in the AI company’s first trading session. (TechCrunch AI)

item.title: A ruler with 12 tick marks per centimeter shows up in three papers — Central South University confirms academic misconduct
item.description: Central South University has confirmed that three questioned papers, flagged because a 1-centimeter scale showed 12 tick marks, involved academic misconduct including fabricated or altered data and images and improper authorship, with the authors demoted. (AIbase)

item.title: OpenAI's first AI hardware targets shipment by end of 2026, with deep involvement from Chinese supply chain partners
item.description: OpenAI's first AI hardware is targeting a end-2026 shipment, with Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile on final assembly, Luxshare Precision handling exclusive assembly and core parts, and a rumored screenless, Jony Ive-linked donut design at $300–400. (AIbase)

item.title: Liu Xiao, who moved from Kuaishou's local life services to Kling AI, has reportedly left Kuaishou
item.description: Liu Xiao, who led Kuaishou's local life business after its September 2025 division upgrade before moving to Kling AI in July 2026 to head commercialization, has reportedly left Kuaishou at E15, with Kling AI not responding. (AIbase)

item.title: Room AI — Talk to it like a designer. Your room, one change at a time
item.description: Despite a headline promising that Room AI lets users "talk to it like a designer" and change a room one step at a time, the page serves only a CAPTCHA security check, with no product features, figures or usage details. (Product Hunt)

item.title: Amidst fears of AI cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’
item.description: Satya Nadella downplayed Microsoft’s recent Outlook outage while warning that much critical infrastructure is “unpatchable,” framing AI as both an opportunity and a new security challenge across the connected world. (TechCrunch AI)

item.title: Why AI Needs to “Localize”—A Conversation with Pete Warden, Founder of Moonshine Voice
item.description: Why AI Needs to “Localize”—A Conversation with Pete Warden, Founder of Moonshine Voice (thedataexchange.media)

item.title: CUHK-Shenzhen and Microsoft Research present ConvexLLM: skipping transcription so audio can tap directly into LLM reasoning
item.description: ConvexLLM, from CUHK-Shenzhen and Microsoft Research, uses a C-Gate architecture mapping speech into the convex hull of frozen text word embeddings via non-negative weighted combinations, skipping transcription to call LLM reasoning directly and avoid intermediate-step information loss and latency. (AIbase)
